reviews.text: 就一张地图 30分钟打完 68块钱？ 怎么敢的呀？？？
首先不可否认很好，然后就是ea你就给1关，现在游戏制作组越来越大胆了，但还是很期待。来呀组队呀

我得深深地为制作组打个问号，请问只有一关的游玩，一局半小时左右，这样就能拿出来卖了？这是谁带来的“好习惯”，将堪比DEMO版本的游戏提前售卖，别人DEMO是为了吸引玩家告诉玩家购入后有更多内容，你个EA敢只有一张图一个BOSS打完告诉你别急还没做完就出来卖？这不得不说是个十分大胆且作死的营销手段。 我确实玩到过只有几章的EA游戏就拿出来卖的，但是别人是剧情策略游戏啊（虽然在几次重做游戏后无果就没动静了），还有个已经成为了陷阱狠狠地欺骗了消费者的剧情游戏D4（不是暗黑破坏神4），你个肉鸽是怎么敢就这样出来的？肉鸽游戏只有第一章就敢出来先EA卖着，让大家伙刷你个第一章刷个50小时？肉鸽游戏见不到深度基本就和自己的热度说再见了啊，你怎么敢？ 我们是游戏玩家还是开独立游戏盲盒玩家还是炒股玩家啊？让我们先投资放着养养到能玩？Steam也是一款大型养成游戏，先买个游戏放库里养着玩是吧，我们玩家还玩不玩游戏了？ 退一步越想越气，你说游戏做的细节不足，能忍，做的深度欠缺，能忍，但是你搞这套，打完第一个BOSS你就告诉我游戏目前结束了？我到底玩的是DEMO还是EA？付费DEMO是吧？ 我就不说你这破游戏里第一张图动不动就遇到奶血的怪，一个不知道是啥的打怪事件里两个奶妈两个狂战士，我一个吹笛子的鼠鼠人，奶妈打不动，近战追着几下把我打残，然后奶妈在嚣张的加血，我真的谢谢你啊。打架打起来六亲不认的，动不动就挨各种伤害还很痛，后面玩了把小红帽，变狼大口大口得吸血才能找回我还只在第一关的感觉，上来就折磨玩家是吧。 手感，美术风格，感觉没有太大问题。但是你这个地图探索式的，玩家还要花时间赶路到各个事件，虽然你传送点设置了很多，但是这赶路是为了啥？只是单纯的区分出自己不是靠“房间选择”来决定发展？只是为了让玩家在路上打几个怪让消磨下玩家时间顺带让玩家获得点经验？让玩家特意花点时间去收集一下资源突显出资源紧迫时间赶人？为了让玩家所谓的可以选择“速跑”还是“发育”？目前的这点游戏内容并不能让玩家看出来这么做的意义，反而是枯燥的赶路让玩家更难受。 ------稍作补充------- 一个肉鸽游戏你不玩build组建搁着品半小时一局的随机事件玩是吧，还什么给差评是随机事件没体验全，收集没集齐。肉鸽你不是组建build逐渐挑战敌人，搁着玩随机事件模拟器是吧，这也能成为抨击差评的一点？ 一个游戏就算流程只有1个小时，只要他能让我乐让我玩的高兴玩的舒服，都是没有问题的。但是这个游戏没有让我玩的高兴玩的舒服，不用几个机制好的角色打起来完完全全就是坐牢，用着好打的角色你也要紧绷神经的去战斗去留意各种东西，正反馈不了一点。 游戏未来可期是未来可期，制作组有口碑良好的前作可以相对放心是没错，但是明明有众筹这种手段却还要发布出来考验自己的信用，我哭死

有些人可能不明白差评的只有一关、只有一章是什么概念， rouge游戏不就是固定的图固定的怪物种类选择吗， 这游戏现在的内容就好比: 英雄联盟里的野区，石头人狼四鸟蛤蟆然后蓝红双BUFF然后小龙最后男爵，就这几个怪拼凑在一个图里，你从最弱的开始打，最后第四天打男爵，打完就没了，重复还是这几只怪，看上去每次位置不同，但实际上你出生点周围还是最弱的，你也只能从最弱的开始刷，甚至可以游戏里只有一个小BOSS和最终BOSS，连红蓝BUFF都没有！只有6个英雄每次就进游戏刷野区，打完男爵就没了， 就好比枪火重生有猫狗鸟虎兔龟但只有古墓第一关，关底只有一种BOSS，没有密室 就好比杀戮尖塔没有遗物，只有一层，两个房间，一个BOSS房，一个本来一层里的那么多房间的怪都混在一个房间里，而杀戮尖塔的四个职业玩法比这游戏6个英雄玩法要多得多,我就不比较了 就好比哈迪斯只有塔尔塔罗斯区域，只有两个房间，一个房里全是遭遇战房里的怪，一个房只有墨纪拉，6种武器撑死两种形态，没有众神祝福只有槌子，那些养成对话啥的就更别想了， 就好比雨中冒险2只有遥远的栖息地，6个职业，打出来的东西只能强化自己的技能. 总而言之就是内容实在太少了....不知道制作组有多缺钱还是有多偷懒才做这么点内容出来
游戏是好玩的 色调是费眼的 内容是不够的 诚意是没有的 缺钱是明显的 差评是得给的
终于找到比我勾8还短的东西了

全角色都通了一遍，感觉可以勉强小评一下，总的来说现在还是 不推荐 纯路人买的 该公司前作《无间冥寺》我也是从最初的ea阶段就入手的，和现在的成品无间相比，ea版本的内容也很少（也只有一关豹神），且缺点也同样较多，但是经过打磨后完整版的无间质量也是属于上乘佳作，这点我就不赘述。所以基于前作，我个人认为该公司是有打算且有能力把鸦卫做好的，且这游戏的底子感觉还行，美术风格奇特，打击感目前还差点反馈。 优点我就不多说了，说说建议吧。翻滚的CD太长了，建议减半或者可以连滚两下，很多大范围技能有点躲不开；翻滚期间不是无敌的，这点我实在有点难理解为什么这么设计，这样翻滚的作用直接减半。部分角色技能硬直过长且不能打断（比如贝奥武夫的旋风斩），建议改成再按一次取消。地图过大了，角色的移速对于跑图来说太慢，效率很低，但是在战斗期间其实还行，建议加入脱战加速机制。升级后选技能期间不会暂停游戏，这点蛮反人类的，建议加紧改掉。晚上的亮度有点过低了，经常看不清路，可摧毁路障和不可摧毁物体感官上几乎没差别，建议可摧毁物体加个反光，可交互物体也顺便加上吧，还有高低差也不是很明显，有地方感觉能上去但是就是上不去，小地图和实际地面的距离感感觉不匹配，感觉抵达小地图上交互点了但实际还差点（这可能是我个人问题，距离感一直不是很好）。完全没有教程（和无间ea一个毛病），引导也几乎没有，速度补上图鉴百科之类的有助于新人上手。 目前就想到这么多，暂时还是不推荐纯新人入手的，玩过前作或者特别喜欢这类画风的可以考虑，第一次写长评，蛮乱的，各位体谅下，也欢迎补充讨论。 （好评是我确实喜欢玩，但我不推荐） 2023/4/7 ———————————————————————————————————————————————————————对于时间限制的处理我觉得可以改为类似无间腐化值的设定，会随时间和特殊事件增长，达到一定阶段后发生突变，然后让玩家从三个突变中自选一个（强烈建议自选，别和无间一样没得选，鸦卫不同角色间的差异较大，不适配的突变很可能导致游戏提前宣判结束，给予玩家十分强烈的挫败感），再不济也改成雨中冒险一样随时间强化怪物，不要僵硬死板地强制玩家搜完全部物资前就开始boss战，应当对效率高的玩家进行奖励而不是对动作慢的玩家进行惩罚。另外麻烦好好解决一下联机匹配卡顿问题，尤其是路人野排，游戏体验很差。 2024/1/7

玩了百把小时，全角色通难4来说说。 各个方面都是一坨。 1.无用的防御，除了转化为攻击想不明白加防御的意义，资源本来就有限，谁会投到防御去。整体容错偏低，基本上是奔着无伤去，防御有什么用，0.6刀灌死我和0.5刀灌死我有区别吗？还是说防御活力拉满就可以跟怪打消耗战？ 2.稀烂的技能组设计。每个角色有多少废物天赋懂得都懂，突出一个各有各的没用，连自己的技能组联动都是一坨，冰女E键可以直接扣掉，贝奥武夫没**会用魔龙特技，更何况一堆辣鸡天赋，狗都不选。初始天赋谁不roll？几个防御天赋纯摆设。你设计了威能 特技 平A不同走向的天赋，干脆让它们互相冲突得了，小红帽特技天赋和威能抢连击点这是人设计得出来的？阿拉丁2级学龙卷或冲锋斩是天胡，学收弯刀可以直接重开。角色技能组不说平衡，你起码不要有废物天赋和互相冲突的天赋吧？我建议你多做几个技能，分流彻底点算了。 3.猴子。这得单独拎出来，稀烂的手感，暴毙的体验，最有特色的一集。威能第一下不免伤，后续又无敌，落地后摇长得能装个小红帽。奔是秒杀流，冲锋斩是爽游，2级拿别的我建议直接重开，别折磨自己。特技打完才能进CD，外圈才有伤害，连诺手内圈刮都有伤害，你个念珠超度自己是吧。 4.平庸的数值设计，像工具人三五四大佬说的，小红帽200块升5%的爆伤，商店75有25%，你有病还是我有病？而且人物属性也不具体，5点伤害到底多大收益，角色多少暴击多少爆伤了，升级加多少属性，全靠蒙，你该计算的不计算，天天惦记你那**倒计时和扣经验，你***。 5.文本校对。这个说烂了，建议回炉。 6.机制问题。最典型的猴子威能，索敌经常错误，要么打一个，要么打一下，圈钱也不是这样圈吧？冰女特质打出的普攻不吃普攻加成，这种小地方你不能说明一下？ 7..折磨玩家。经验和时间一砍再砍，现在连偷矿都不行，经典设计师教育玩家，以下克上了嗷。把把玩得心惊胆战，又算时间又算路线，这不是高难度，这是纯恶心，搭配上各方面的机制、数值问题，这不叫硬核，这就是纯粹一坨，纯恶心人。我问问你工作室的几个能通关？你玩个阿拉丁2级回收弯刀，3级学回血，4级学附魔点你能过第一个boss？别是自己难2都打不过在这儿折磨玩家吧。

正式版，新改动再一次超出我的预期，是的，又削了玩家的伤害。乘算道具暗改成加法，而敌人的伤害一点都没削，后期敌人一刀砍你半血轻轻松松。传奇/诅咒道具的获取也砍，玩家后期难以成型已是家常便饭。 最终BOSS，纯召唤+弹幕+全场AOE，没有无敌帧技能？那就死呗！ 请各位想入手的看这里！建议先去看看研发直播打游戏的录像，你大概知道这整个团队是什么样的水平 我从来没想过每次的平衡调整，都是根据研发收集一群低难度玩家的反馈和臆想高难度玩家的体验，来瞎调整的。 永远都是砍角色数值和道具数值，加高敌人伤害和机制。搁那玩魂游？ 你自己做的游戏，自己通过关吗，但凡难度高一点通关过一次都不会做出这种弱智调整。 全面调高所有商品价格！本来上个版本玩法单一的主要问题就是前中期钱不够，导致道具只能选择和钱挂钩的。你现在还加价，玩家可选道具就更少了。 三村的敌人各种多段攻击，你个游戏，冲刺又没无敌帧，你想让玩家怎么躲！还加强敌人的机动性。咋地，隔壁黄金树给了你灵感？敌人可以无脑堆数值和机动性？ 2个多月，BUG没修几个，没新增内容，就寻思怎么不让玩家通关？

unnecessarily addicted to this game. this game is very hard and punishing, and i feel that most of the negative reviews that points out how unfair this game is have perfect sense. but that is exactly the kind of dopamine my brain craves. this game rewards resilient players, those who are patient in learning the enemies kit, moveset, patterns, and weakness. you need curiosity to experiment with the characters kit, builds, combinations, and if you are playing coop with friends, synergies with other characters. i am close at 100%-ing this game, and i can say for sure that this game is perfectly balanced, with a very wide spectrum in both side of the scale. perfect build makes you dominate the entire run, while a weak build punishes you hard for the entire run. but still, remember that this is a roguelike game, meaning that rng exists and not all of your runs will be perfect. you will lose a lot, and that is totally normal. the key is to understanding what makes a good run, and the journey to that knowledge will reward your brain with dopamine handsomely.

Great game ruined by absolutely awful balancing Ravenswatch has strong characters, satisfying combat, and a genuinely good foundation. Unfortunately, the balancing is such an unbearable pile of ♥♥♥♥ that none of it matters. Two-player co-op, especially from Darkness difficulty onward, is pure frustration. You are constantly forced to rush because of the timer, desperately hunt for the perfect items, and hope your build somehow produces enough damage. There is no room to experiment, take your time, or simply enjoy the game. Either you snowball immediately or the entire run is basically dead. Instead of feeling challenging, it feels unfair, stressful, and exhausting. Every session ended with rage rather than fun. There is a genuinely great game buried underneath all of this, but the co-op balancing completely ruins it. 1/5 — fun gameplay trapped inside a frustration simulator.

This game is seriously underrated, and I will try to explain why: - it is very well polished on all levels, from sound to UI, VFX are very clean and readable and user friendly; - action combat is very good, it gets you in a flow and although not there, it is close to the best in the genre (among those I've played) - Hades - 55 hours in, 90% of which coop, we didn't have a single significant technical issue And now the unique elements: - characters are really unique, not just as numbers or different ways to do the same, but they are played in hugely different manner, which deserves a lot of respect; Playing with Melusine, Geppetto and Aladdin feels like playing three different games; a lot of creativity went into that and balance is also good enough - it is multiplayer; I can't recall other action roguelike with that quality and pace to provide a meaningful multiplayer; we can at least say they are not many games like this - map control running against time; it gives a whole new perspective on things, a strategy layer and requires adaptiveness, especially in multiplayer, where the possibilities are much more (not just what and when, but splits and rejoining) Frankly, if this is the type of game you want, I cannot see how you can give a negative review and it is very clear what it will provide, so I wouldn't expect many misguided souls to end up playing it more than 2H. Find friends to play, give it a try, if you don't want to have very hard time, stay away from Nightmare difficulty.

With 300+ hours in the game, I can confidently say that if you like rogue-likes or even action RPGs, this should be an instant buy for you. It's outstanding! Most of the characters are really fun and interesting to play, though there are some you absolutely should not start with (Scarlet, Geppetto, looking at you....). Each character has at least a couple of really strong builds that are fun, and even if you have bad luck with RNG on your items, you can still clear content on all difficulties. The maps for each chapter are unique and fun, and there's enough variety that they feel unique. There's a day/night system that makes certain enemies much more preferable to fight in one phase or the other (e.g. killing trees during the night makes them spawn several spiders you have to kill but not during the day). This impacts your choices and how you want to path through the maps and when you want to go where, once you learn what areas things tend to spawn in. This leads me to the biggest downside the game currently has: there's a significant learning curve (map strategy, map points of interest, character builds, enemies, items for builds, etc.), and the game doesn't really help you learn a lot of the really important aspects at all. Without that understanding, the game may be very frustrating to new players who might struggle. To get that knowledge, I personally recommend a youtube channel called Positive4ce. He's SUPER helpful and does a great job explaining characters, map strategy, and builds. Start with his video titled "How To Run The Map In Ravenswatch" for a crash course that will make your start MUCH better. If you want a more in-depth walkthrough of the thought process, watch his video called "How To Get Better At Ravenswatch | Run review". All in all, it's a phenomenal game, and it's so cheap (especially when on sale, as low as around $10!), the value you can get out of it is tremendous. Super, super fun.

It is great to add new content but this feature should be top priority as solving every bug can be quite hard, but allow players wait for their mate to rejoin is a safeguard. I cannot recommend this game as multiplayer is a core feature, and bugs have been there since launch and before without having a mitigation available to players.

Cool game idea but poorly executed. It's my first game review ever. I bought this game with one of my friend and was expecting some fun co-op gaming experiences. But it ends up frustrated both of us. The control system is somehow counter-intuitive. For example ESC button leads to another menu when I just want to quit the map or a conversation. A lot of bugs make the game flow unsatisfying. The hardness is heavily based on luck. It's the most frustrating part. At first, we thought we might need some time to build the character up. But even at the MAX level of a character, you can still get very trashy build due to RNG. And to be honest, it is not fun. Sometimes half way through one game, we just realized we are not going to make it because of the trashy build we've got. It somehow feels like playing some online PVP games with a bunch of random noobs. We did our best, but the rng failed us. I know there are guides online that we can use to help us through. But I'd like to explore a game myself. If any games are designed to play with a guide. I, unfortunately, am not the player of those. I'm personally very disappointed at the game. It gives me rollercoaster feelings and I don't like it when it is going down. All I would say is, it is not the game for me. I had some fun moments. But the frustrations killed it all.

Ok, the game has a lot of good features going for it. The characters are great, the power fantasies given through each of them is absolutely fantastic, the personality of each of them is well written and the overall experience is quite fun if you choose to look past a great deal of things the devs just want you to sort of "deal with". It can be clearly seen that the developers put a lot of heart into the project. And even though I recommend the game I have some issues with it that make the game unnecessarily stressful, and annoying and take some level of player expression out of it, and, in my opinion takes a lot out of the experience: First the game doesn't let you play as several copies of the same character. I understand that the narrative doesn't support it, but being so focused on quick gameplays the story aspects kind of swing past you, even on the lowest of difficulties. So if you and your friends have that sweet DLC and you want to play as the same character, well tough luck, you're gonna have to play turns. And if you're solo queueing, it can get even more annoying to be sort of competing for a character in a game where there isn't any type of competition. Second, the hourglass.. That darned thing. Yes I understand the devs want to make the game fast-paced, and setting a night and day cycle is great for the gameplay, but having to run around the map without getting too much of a chance of enjoying the combat, or having the time to plan different strategies, or just standing around to calmly think about your next step makes the whole game feel like you're in a constant rush every single time. So if you want to calmly enjoy the side quests there's no chance to do it and earn goodies and levels for your characters... You're just more likely skipping everything you see in favour of just min-maxing your stats and abilities to get the most bang for your buck and running to the finish line as quickly as you can. And maybe AFTER you leveled up your character you can try slower runs through modifiers that don't let you earn experience. Third, solo queueing is a very complicated experience to enjoy, but playing with others is sort of a must if you wish to earn the most amount of powerups and in-game resources. My issue doesn't lie with the multiplayer aspect in itself, but instead with the lack of management tools one gets while playing with a full team of unknown people that muted their mics and audio, but still get the chance to drag to wherever they want, if they get there before you, all while spamming a single signal in the map, which is the only non vocal tool given to the players. There is no chat, there is no emotes, and no way to stop someone from starting a "story" bossfight right as you were getting a chest item, which would result in some frustration and you losing a possible item choice that could benefit your gameplay. And since the regular game mode is not really recommended to play solo (although it is absolutely possible). The multiplayer aspect is highly recommended to be played alongside people you know, or have a voice chat to communicate through. And last, but certainly not least, the roguelike mechanics. For a roguelike game as Ravenswatch tries to be, the biomes themselves feel extremely limited. Making the whole sidequesting mechanic part of the different "biomes" you get to experience inside the main biomes themselves. But then again they can feel immensely limited by the fast pace of a run if there's a player leading the charge and going to different places than you want to be. And that paired with the players that just seem to be speedrunning when they play with you makes the linear sequence of biomes feel even shorter than it already is. If possible, I'd try to give players more options of "worlds" to explore, as well as more time to explore them without punishing them too hard for trying to savour the experience at their own pace. Overall, the game experience is fun, I loved the Merlin character DLC. He feels amazing to play as. But I find myself just leaving the game for months after a couple of successful runs due to all these issues. Even though my comments might seem mostly negative, I must say that I have enjoyed the experience so far, but would need some more improvements to it to make me want to keep playing for longer sessions without feeling so tired afterwards. If you read this review to the end I thank you so much for your time. If you're curious about buying the game and supporting the franchise, please do give it a chance. The game is a lot of fun, but just needs some improvements.

Solid 7/10 - has very interesting ideas, pretty unique gameplay loop where you have multiple objectives each map, each with randomized difficulty which and the heroes and powerups are almost all very fun. The gameplay loop is engaging enough to play with the flaws, but the game really lacks variety. As you play you advance through three maps, all the same each time. For the price tag I'd kinda expect each level to have at least a pool of two maps to choose from. For each hero more talents are added to the pool as you level up the hero (outside of the run), but I think you level up heroes WAY too slowly - if you are used to play on other heroes on higher difficulties and want to play something unleveled, you have to slog through tons of uncompletable runs just to unlock more talents for that specific champ. One full hour Nightmare defeated run can sometimes not even give you a full level, while chessing levels by adding all affixes and abandoning after level 2 + boss fight give you the same XP in 3 minutes. The hero abilities and builds are clearly the best part of the game, but even here there are some choices I don't quite understand, such as giving some heroes full animation lock / self stuns on spells which can get you instakilled by bad luck. Playing around this is very unfun. The game can be quite advanced in strats for a roguelike, to the point where I'd wish some things were explained a bit better in-game as to not require the wiki as often Music/SFX, artstyle and overall vibe are very nice
